summary.headline: Ola Electric Q1 FY27 deliveries nearly doubled QoQ to ~39,200 units, Auto revenue ₹455 crore (+72% QoQ), Auto gross margin 30.5%.
summary.overview: Ola returned to volume growth in Q1 FY27, with deliveries of ~39,200 units (nearly 2x QoQ) and orders of ~44,000, while electric two-wheeler registrations grew 97% against a market up ~17% QoQ, lifting share from 5.1% to 8.4%. Auto revenue rose 72% QoQ to ₹455 crore with gross profit of ₹139 crore and Auto gross margin held at 30.5%. Consolidated opex fell 22% QoQ to ₹333 crore (including a ~₹55 crore one-time reversal of a Cell ACC PLI penalty provision), and adjusted operating EBITDA improved to –₹195 crore from –₹326 crore in Q4 FY26. Management pivoted Auto distribution from company-owned to a multi-channel model with dealers, with the first batch slated to go live on Janmashtami (4 September), and reiterated a Cell gigafactory ramp to 6 GWh.

financial_highlights.change: -22% QoQ from ₹428 crore in Q4; ~₹380 crore excluding ~₹55 crore one-time PLI provision reversal
from 5.1%; Ola registrations +97% QoQ vs market ~+17%

segments.name: Auto (scooters, motorcycles)
segments.commentary: Revenue ₹455 crore (+72% QoQ), gross profit ₹139 crore, gross margin 30.5%. Premium business recovering; motorcycles starting to grow in northern plains. Roadster a small minority of sales; 9.1 kWh variant supply constrained by 4680 cell shortage.

segments.name: Cell business
segments.commentary: 4680 NMC cells commercially deployed; a few hundred thousand cells produced and in customer vehicles. Production paused in Q1 to take capacity from 2.5 GWh to 6 GWh; restart expected later in August. 46100 LFP cell BIS-certified. Yields high-70s to ~80% at pause, target >90% within a quarter of restart.

segments.name: Ola Shakti / Mahashakti (energy storage)
segments.commentary: Only a few hundred NMC-based Shakti units delivered in Q1, no meaningful revenue; NMC version pared back on sub-target margins. Shakti Gen 2 (LFP) to be announced 15 August. First Mahashakti MoU with Axis Energy for 20 GWh over 5-6 years; early Mahashakti revenue hoped for Q3 or Q4.

guidance_outlook: Auto ASP to stay broadly around ₹1.25 lakh, plus or minus 5%.
Auto gross margin target ~30-32%; expected to hold above 30% over next one to two quarters and improve as commodity prices ease.
Opex to fall to ₹300-325 crore range over the next couple of quarters.
Gross margin steady to slightly growing and volumes steady to slightly growing while cutting opex; no formal FY volume guidance.

Gigafactory at 6 GWh to be fully commissioned in Q1 FY27 quarter (also stated as operational by September); expansion from 6 GWh to 20 GWh (prismatic) targeted in FY27, funded by Cell-company equity rather than parent equity.
Service revenue target ~₹400-500 crore by FY2027-28 from installed base of over one million customers.
Capex beyond Cell project about ₹30-50 crore; ₹50 crore used as target number.
Pending 4680-cell Roadster deliveries to be completed over Q2 and Q3 FY27.
capex_capacity: Cell capacity: 2.5 GWh installed, production paused for ~2-3 months to take capacity to 6 GWh; installation expected to finish within a week to ten days, with restart later in August.
Auto factory scaled to ~1 million units per year; no material Auto capex foreseen.
Remaining Cell capex funded through debt; equity contribution largely complete.
Ongoing capex beyond Cell project ~₹30-50 crore; ₹50 crore used as target.
Prismatic cell R&D expected complete by end of CY2026; 6 to 20 GWh expansion intended to be equity-funded at the Cell company.
Depreciation policy aligned to industry norms, causing ~₹10-20 crore delta.
demand_pricing: Ola registrations +97% QoQ vs electric 2W market +17%; share 5.1% to 8.4%; growth across all regions.
Electric 2W penetration in India crossed 10% for the first time in June 2026.
ASP fell sharply QoQ, ~90% due to product mix; premium scooter sales recovering.

Dealer model: ~500 current touchpoints (analyst figure); company stores to become fewer, larger experience centres; ~1,000 expressions of interest from prospective dealers; 20-30 dealers engaged for about a month before announcement.
Service challenges attributed to parts availability (vendor issues, geopolitical factors); dealers to stock parts on cash-and-carry basis.
Shakti to be sold through company stores, automotive dealers and industry-specific inverter/battery channels.

qa_highlights.question: Why did ASP decline sharply sequentially?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed about 90% to product mix; ASP guided at ~₹1.25 lakh ±5%.

qa_highlights.question: Full-year volume guidance and Q4 exit rate?
qa_highlights.answer: No formal guidance; management expects steady growth but declined quarter-on-quarter numbers.

qa_highlights.question: Own-cell penetration and Shakti revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: A few thousand own-cell vehicles on road; about 3 of ~9-10 SKUs use 4680 cells. Shakti Gen 1 (NMC) had no meaningful revenue; Gen 2 (LFP) on 15 August.

qa_highlights.question: Capex for the year?
qa_highlights.answer: Beyond the Cell project, capex ~₹30-50 crore, with ₹50 crore as target; Auto needs hardly any capex.

qa_highlights.question: Why did depreciation fall QoQ?
qa_highlights.answer: Policy aligned to industry norms after aggressive depreciation; delta ~₹10-20 crore, no write-off mentioned.

qa_highlights.question: LFP vs NMC mix and 20 GWh expansion timing?
qa_highlights.answer: Almost all Auto to move to LFP over time, ~20% of Auto stays NMC; Shakti/Mahashakti all LFP. 20 GWh expansion (prismatic) in FY27 with separate Cell-company equity; yields high-70s to ~80% at pause.

qa_highlights.question: Scale of energy storage opportunity and Axis Energy MoU?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cites CEA estimate of ~400 GWh needed over 5-6 years, which it views as an underestimate; Mahashakti expected to have round-trip efficiency a few points above peers and safety above standard 5 MWh containers.

qa_highlights.question: Roadster contribution?
qa_highlights.answer: Small minority of sales; deliveries slightly below orders in Q1 due to 4680 cell shortage.
